Background rebuilt on the causes frame so it matches its sibling, the approach frame, two rows down the same carousel. THE SUBJECT IS UNTOUCHED — every pixel of the block, the plate and the tissue is the approved frame, byte for byte. Only the background around it is replaced.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, MEASURED RATHER THAN EYEBALLED. A contrast-boosted view of the background field showed four faults, three of them left by this frame's own earlier post-processing:
  RECTANGULAR SEAM   a hard-edged rectangle roughly 220..1800 x 200..1890, the boundary of the
                     Laplace inpaint done on 2026-08-26. Visible as a straight-sided box of
                     slightly different tone around the block.
  HALO RING          a bright glow hugging the block on all sides, brightest top-centre
  STRAY DARK BLOB    an unexplained dark patch in the bottom-right corner, unattached to anything
  VIGNETTE           corners falling away unevenly — top-left L182 against bottom-left L243, a
                     61-level spread across a background that should read as one colour

DONE DETERMINISTICALLY, NOT WITH A MASKED AI EDIT. A mask is a permission, not a constraint: an engine given one redraws the silhouette, and this block's layer stack is the whole content of the picture. Everything below is arithmetic.

HOW THE NEW GROUND WAS BUILT, AND IT IS THE APPROACH FRAME'S OWN. A 2D quartic surface was fitted per channel to the approach frame's background, with four robust re-fits rejecting dark outliers so its cast shadow and its two detached spheres were excluded from the model rather than averaged into it. The recorded polynomial trap on this repo is extrapolation into UNSAMPLED corners; here every corner is sampled and the surface is only ever evaluated inside the frame, so that trap does not apply. Fitted corners came out TL 201.5, TR 200.9, BL 249.3, BR 179.8 — within a couple of levels of direct samples off the same frame, which is the check that the fit is real.

THE CAST SHADOW IS THE APPROACH FRAME'S REAL ONE, MOVED. It was lifted as a multiplicative ratio of the approach frame against its own fitted surface, so it is the photographed shadow and not a synthesised ellipse. It was then windowed to the plate region and feathered to nothing at its borders, scaled 0.817 in x (the causes plate is 1442px wide against the approach's 1764) and translated so its top edge meets the causes plate bottom at y=1671.

FOUR THINGS WENT WRONG ON THE WAY AND ARE WORTH WRITING DOWN:
  1  PLATE FOUND BY THE WRONG RULE. Taking the object mask's bottom-most row picked a 120px
     sliver where the mask had leaked into the shadow, giving an x-scale of 12.0. The plate is
     the WIDEST row of the object, not the lowest one.
  2  HARD EDGES FROM THE WARP. Filling outside the source with a constant, and the mask leak
     itself, both landed as straight lines across the finished background. Windowing the
     shadow and feathering it to 1.0 before warping is what removes them.
  3  A BRIGHT HOLE INSIDE THE WEDGE, where the approach mask had leaked into its own shadow —
     it read as a pale patch at lower left. A grey opening removes small bright details and
     leaves the wedge intact.
  4  A SLAB, NOT A SHADOW. At native pixels the transplant had a hard top edge and a blocky
     right end. A 45px blur is what turns it back into light falling off. None of these were
     visible in the downscaled view — all four were found at 100%.

THE HALO RING NEEDED THE MASK TIGHTENING. The structure mask picks up the halo too, because a
glow has a gradient like anything else; left in, it survived as a white fringe against the new
ground. Eroding 13px stops the mask at the block's real edge. Checked rather than assumed: the
bbox moved 323..1766 to 329..1755 in x and 382..1679 to 389..1668 in y, so the erosion took the
ring and not the block.

TWO VERSIONS WERE MADE because Malcolm's instruction admits two readings and the difference is
visible. This plan publishes A. B is built, sits beside it in publish-ready, and is one command
away:
  A  smooth ground + the cast shadow — 'the same background as the approach image', which has one
  B  smooth ground, no shadow anywhere — the most literal reading of 'a smooth even colour'

NEW FILENAME, NEVER A RE-UPLOAD: Shopify Files suffixes a name collision and keeps serving the
original. Checked this stem is not a prefix of any live file and none is a prefix of it — the
closest live names are skingenetix-fine-lines-wrinkles-collagen-elastin-damage-cross-section and
...-crows-feet-mature-skin, and both diverge at 'fine-lines-c' against 'fine-lines-w'.

SQUARE 2048x2048 PRESERVED — media-with-text sets its row height from the master's own aspect,
so the file must stay 1:1 or this block grows taller than its siblings. Under the 3000px cap, so
uploaded at native size with metadata stripped, q95 4:4:4, and not re-compressed.

THE OUTGOING FILE STAYS UPLOADED AND UNREFERENCED, as does every earlier iteration of this frame
